messages:
Kai Chan: Heads-up — I'm seeing a cluster of requests where the routing eval returned `no_match` even though `X-Customer-ID` is present. Low volume but persistent for ~6 hours.
Maria V: any chance this is sampling? which route?
Kai Chan: It's hitting the `/v1/generate` API, tenant-based header rules. Example incoming header: `X-Customer-ID: cust_42`. Decision log shows `rule_id: null` in a bunch of traces.
Ben R: ops-bot alerted us earlier about increased `route_eval_latency`. Could be a race in header normalization + eval sampler dropping the span.
ops-bot: [alert] route_eval_no_match spike on region-us-west — 120 events in the last 30m. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd
Zoe: Can you paste the routing config snippet? want to see match predicates and header transforms.
Kai Chan: Sure — here's the rule (redacted):
```json
{
  "id": "route-customer-tenant",
  "match": {
    "path": "/v1/generate",
    "headers": [
      {"name": "X-Customer-ID", "present": true}
    ]
  },
  "actions": {"backend": "dedicated-pool-1"}
}
```
Maria V: That looks fine. Two hypotheses: 1) header name normalization (x-customer-id vs X-Customer-ID) + evaluation sampling that decides not to emit a decision log, or 2) the sampler is deterministic but was using a key that wasn't stable (like IP) and the test traffic changes.
Ben R: We recently lowered global decision-log sampling to 0.05 for cost reasons. If the sampler runs before header normalization, many matches will be skipped in logs even though routing succeeded.
Zoe: Repro steps? Kai, can you curl with exact headers and attach `x-request-id` so we can follow a trace?
Kai Chan: Repro below. I can see the gateway returned 200 and backend used dedicated pool, but decision log entry missing for match.
```
curl -H "X-Customer-ID: cust_42" -H "x-request-id: test-req-123" https://api.redwood/v1/generate
```
Maria V: I pushed a temporary flip to increase decision-log sampling to 0.5 for `/v1/*` in us-west for 30m (toggle: `routing.decision_logging.sampling.override.us-west.api.v1 = 0.5`). Should show more traces in ~2mins.
Ben R: Long-term we should make sampling inclusive of routes with header-based predicates or use a deterministic sample key that includes `x-request-id` or `X-Customer-ID`. Want to avoid silent gaps.
Zoe: Agree. Proposal: add a 'must_log' flag to rules where predicate uses sensitive headers (customer id, org id) so the sampler always emits at least 1/1000. Also add a Grafana panel showing `decision_log_emit_rate` by route+predicate_type.
Kai Chan: After Maria's flip I see several decision logs appear with header normalization mismatch: header was `x-customer-id` lowercase in request and our evaluator was checking case-sensitively in one path. Fixing a small normalizer bug now.
Ben R: Great catch. Still want the deterministic-sampling PR: sampler should hash `{route_id}:{x-request-id||trace_id||client_ip}` so we get stable coverage. I'll open a draft.
Maria V: Dashboard work item created: D-3498 "Decision log coverage heatmap by route/header-predicate".
Zoe: Also adding an alert rule: if route reports 0 decision logs for >5m while traffic >100r/m, fire a critical.
Kai Chan: Patch to header normalizer pushed to canary; rolling out to us-west now. Will monitor decision-log emit count.
Ben R: Thanks — once canary is green, please backfill a tiny sampling bump for last 2h so we can reconstruct missed evals for the postmortem.
ops-bot: [deploy] canary deploy started by Kai Chan — deploy-456. ETA 3m.
Kai Chan: Canary looks clean after 10m, decision logs coming in for previously-missing requests. Leaving the sampling override in place for 30m to collect more data.
Maria V: Filing follow-up: 1) deterministic sampler RFC, 2) 'must_log' rule flag, 3) dashboard + alert. I'll assign owners.
Ben R: I'll pair on the RFC.
Zoe: I'll take the dashboard.
Kai Chan: Thanks all, closing the short loop. :thumbsup:
